item.title: Scientists say land-preservation costs should be factored into agrivoltaics’ LCOE calculations
item.description: German researchers found that agrivoltaics costs far exceed agricultural benefits, raising doubts about subsidies and highlighting the need for more cost-competitive system designs.

item.title: Energy Vault secures 1.5 GWh sodium-ion supply for AI
item.description: Switzerland-based Energy Vault has secured an initial 1.5 GWh of sodium-ion battery supply from Peak Energy to develop integrated storage systems for artificial intelligence-focused data centers.

item.title: Varta unveils residential battery with AI-driven energy management
item.description: The Germany battery manufacturer is expanding its portfolio with a modularly scalable LFP storage solution featuring a new energy management system. The new product comes with the company’s proprietary “Varta.iq” software, which is designed to detect consumption anomalies, integrate dynamic electricity tariffs, and enable bidirectional charging.

item.title: Work begins on Georgia’s first utility-scale solar plant for on-site consumption
item.description: The First Light project is billed as the first industrial-scale solar power plant built entirely for self-consumption in the South Caucasus region.

item.title: SolarEdge ships US-made inverters to Europe, ramping up BESS manufacturing
item.description: Single-phase inverter products manufactured in Texas are now being shipped to multiple European markets as SolarEdge adapts its international export strategy. The manufacturer tells pv magazine key components will increasingly be manufactured in the United States in the coming years.

item.title: French startup launches app to boost collective self-consumption
item.description: French startup Jane Energie has introduced a software platform to automate and manage collective self-consumption projects, targeting 100 kWp to 500 kWp installations as the segment moves from feed-in tariffs toward shared local consumption models.

item.title: Pace Digitek secures 250 MW of solar and 1.1 GWh of storage in India
item.description: Karnataka Renewable Energy Development Ltd. (KREDL)) has issued a letter of award to Pace Digitek for a 250 MW solar project with a 250 MW, 1.1 GWh battery energy storage system (BESS) at Pavagada Solar Park in Karnataka, India, with an interim tariff of INR 5.51 ($0.061)/kWh adopted by the Karnataka Electricity Regulatory Commission.

item.title: Brazil reserve battery auction rules near finalization with 20 GW lined up
item.description: Brazil’s electricity regulator has approved March reserve capacity auctions for thermal and hydro plants with more than 125 GW registered, while guidelines for a separate battery storage auction remain pending even as over 20 GW of projects are under development.

item.title: Hungary launches grants for residential battery storage
item.description: Hungary has opened applications for a program offering up to HUF 2.5 million ($7,820) per household to support residential battery storage, prioritizing grid-exporting solar users and small rural settlements.

item.title: Comparing safety profiles of lithium-ion, sodium-ion and solid-state batteries
item.description: New research finds that battery safety rankings are not universal but highly dependent on application scenarios, and shows that LFP batteries can emit high levels of hydrogen fluoride, challenging their reputation as the “safest” chemistry.
